target.title: fix(auto-reply): support custom silent tokens with digits and punctuation in prefix matcher
target.body:
Fixes #99982

## What Problem This Solves

`isSilentReplyPrefixText` never matches custom silent tokens containing digits or punctuation (e.g., `NO_REPLY2`, `HELP-QUIET`). The character guard `/[^A-Z_]/.test(normalized)` rejects any input containing non-letter chars, causing streamed prefix detection to fail for custom tokens with digits/hyphens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guard checked the **input fragment** instead of the **token**. Custom tokens with non-letter chars cannot be mistaken for natural language, so their prefixes are safe once the prefix includes a non-letter char from the token.

## User Impact

Before: custom silent tokens like `"NO_REPLY2"` never match in the streaming prefix matcher.

After: prefix fragments containing a non-letter character from the token (e.g., `"NO_"` for `"NO_REPLY2"`, `"HELP-"` for `"HELP-QUIET"`) are correctly recognized. Pure-letter prefixes like `"HE"` for `"HELP-QUIET"` are still rejected.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: streaming prefix matching for custom silent tokens with digits/punctuation
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/silent-prefix-digits-99982`
- Commands run after this patch:

```
pnpm test src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

Console output from self-contained Node script simulating character-by-character streaming:

```

------+----------------+---------

 wait  | "NO"            | no - waiting for more chars
 MATCH | "NO_"           | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_R"          | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_RE"         | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_REP"        | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_REPL"       | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_REPLY"      | yes - streaming detected
 MATCH | "NO_REPLY2"     | yes - streaming detected

--- Hyphen token: "HELP-QUIET" ---
 Step | Prefix         | Matches?
------+----------------+---------
 wait  | "H"             | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "HE"            | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "HEL"           | no - waiting for more chars
 wait  | "HELP"          | no - waiting for more chars

 Step | Prefix         | Matches?
------+----------------+---------
 wait  | "S"             | no - waiting for more chars
```

target.title: [AI-assisted] fix(cli): surface session lane busy exits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #54622.

A same-session `openclaw agent` CLI dispatch can sit behind an active session lane and fail without telling the operator why. The command queue already has lane-wait diagnostics, but the Gateway/CLI path did not surface them as a structured result. This PR makes CLI-triggered lane waits return a deterministic `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` result instead of a silent generic failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the queue ordering model intact and makes the CLI path opt in to terminal busy rejection when it is waiting behind an active same-session lane. It adds typed wait details, a `rejectOnWait` queue hook, an `AgentSessionLaneBusyError` helper, Gateway response propagation, Swift/protocol response model fields, CLI text/JSON rendering, and tests across queue, Gateway, CLI relay, and embedded-runner lane handling.

This refresh also preserves current-main queue timeout cleanup behavior: `taskTimeoutAbortSignal`, `taskTimeoutAbortGraceMs`, `taskTimeoutReleaseSignal`, and matching `QueueEntry` wiring remain carried through so timed-out embedded runs do not keep lanes held longer than intended.

The compatibility repair removes the transient `sourceCliLaneBusyRejection` Gateway agent request parameter from the CLI request, strict protocol schema, and generated Swift request model. Gateway now derives CLI-only busy rejection from the existing Gateway client identity or mode. Non-CLI Gateway agent calls remain unopted, and upgraded CLIs no longer send an unknown strict v4 request field to older daemons.

## User Impact

Operators now get a clear session-lane busy message and retry suggestion when a second CLI dispatch targets a session lane that is already busy. JSON-mode callers receive structured `errorCode: "LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED"` details. Non-CLI agent runs and normal successful CLI runs keep the existing behavior.

Mixed-version Gateway-backed CLI calls no longer fail solely because an upgraded CLI sends `sourceCliLaneBusyRejection` to an older strict v4 Gateway. Older daemons may still lack the new lane-busy behavior, but they are not rejected for an unknown agent request parameter.

No new dependencies, config, credentials, network surfaces, or queue policy changes are introduced.

target.title: fix(gateway): truncateCloseReason drops partial UTF-8 code point instead of emitting mojibake
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`truncateCloseReason` truncated WebSocket close reasons at a raw byte boundary using `Buffer.subarray(0, maxBytes)`. When `maxBytes` fell inside a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence, Node decoded the dangling continuation bytes as `U+FFFD` replacement characters each 3 bytes wide. This meant:

1. The re-encoded result could exceed `maxBytes`, breaking the RFC 6455 123-byte close-reason limit.
2. Clients received garbled close reason text containing 😀 characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix backs up from `maxBytes` to the nearest UTF-8 sequence start before slicing. UTF-8 continuation bytes match the bit pattern `10xxxxxx` (`byte & 0xC0 === 0x80`); we skip them to land on a sequence-start byte, then slice cleanly.

## User Impact

WebSocket close reasons are now guaranteed to stay within `maxBytes` when re-encoded and never contain replacement characters. The RFC 6455 123-byte limit is reliably enforced for callers using the 120-byte default.

## Evidence

Repro (from issue):

```js
// Before fix
const out = truncateCloseReason("x".repeat(118) + "😀".repeat(5));
Buffer.byteLength(out); // 121 — exceeds 120-byte cap
out.includes(""); // true — mojibake

// After fix
Buffer.byteLength(out); // 118 — within cap
out.includes(""); // false
```

Tests added in `src/gateway/server/close-reason.test.ts` (new file, 7 cases):
- ASCII-only truncation still cuts at exactly `maxBytes`
- 4-byte emoji cut: was 121 bytes, now 118
- 2-byte Latin extended cut (é)
- 3-byte BMP cut (✓)
- Custom `maxBytes` respected

```
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  28 passed (28)
  Duration  1.00s
```

Closes #99976

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw Talk already has a realtime provider contract and gateway-relay path, but the bundled xAI plugin did not expose Grok Voice Agent as a native realtime voice provider.

Without this, users who want xAI/Grok voice in OpenClaw either cannot use it through Talk or have to fall back to a lower-quality STT -> model -> TTS loop. That is especially limiting for long-running assistants where supplier choice and realtime voice cost matter.

Closes #99087.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one canonical bundled xAI realtime voice provider through the existing Talk `gateway-relay` contract instead of creating a separate voice stack.

The provider:

- connects to xAI realtime voice (`grok-voice-latest`) over WebSocket;
- registers through the existing `registerRealtimeVoiceProvider` seam;
- exposes the provider through the xAI plugin manifest;
- maps audio, transcript, tool-call, cancellation, reconnect, and close events into the existing Talk realtime bridge contract;
- keeps secrets out of docs and evidence.

The follow-up commits address the ClawSweeper/Codex review findings:

- interrupted assistant audio now sends `response.cancel` plus `conversation.item.truncate`;
- relay playback cancellation preserves the assistant item until truncation is possible;
- assistant transcript deltas are buffered so delta-only xAI completion still emits a final transcript;
- xAI `input_audio_transcription.updated` events are treated as cumulative replacements and emitted once on completion;
- provider-managed reconnects no longer replay initial `onReady`/greeting callbacks;
- startup WebSocket errors remain terminal instead of leaving background retry loops.

Dependency note: `ws` is intentionally moved into the xAI runtime dependency set because the new provider imports it at runtime. The repository dependency guard correctly requires maintainer/security approval for the exact head SHA or a maintainer-owned regeneration path. This PR does not try to bypass that policy.

## User Impact

Users selecting xAI realtime Talk get native Grok voice replies through the existing OpenClaw Talk relay path rather than a synthetic STT/TTS loop.

Expected behavior:

- Talk can select `provider: "xai"` with `transport: "gateway-relay"`.
- Gateway-relay clients can stream mic audio and receive Grok voice audio.
- Barge-in cancels the active response and truncates only the currently interrupted assistant audio.
- Completed assistant audio and previous-turn assistant items are not truncated on later turns.

target.title: fix(cron): allow timeoutSeconds: 0 for no-timeout mode
target.body:
## 🐛 Problem

The cron job UI validation logic incorrectly rejects `timeoutSeconds: 0`, which should represent "no timeout" mode.

**Current behavior:**
```typescript
if (timeout <= 0) {
  errors.timeoutSeconds = "cron.errors.timeoutInvalid";
}
```
This prevents users from setting `timeoutSeconds = 0` to disable timeout entirely.

## ✅ Solution

Update validation to allow `0` as a valid value (meaning "no timeout"):

```typescript
// 0 = no timeout, > 0 = timeout in seconds
if (timeout !== 0 && timeout <= 0) {
  errors.timeoutSeconds = "cron.errors.timeoutInvalid";
}
```

target.title: fix(mattermost): backfill thread history from server when in-memory window is empty
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint before building inbound context. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without adding repeated thread-history requests to normal same-session follow-ups.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts`: 73 passed; covers stable `route.sessionKey`, stored thread `sessionId` rotation, same-session no-refetch, failed-fetch no-retry, and reset-session refetch.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`: passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.test.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor.inbound-system-event.test.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Live proof: local Docker Mattermost Team Edition 10.11.21 at `http://localhost:8065`, with tokens and Mattermost ids redacted. The proof used real Mattermost REST auth, posts, and `/api/v4/posts/<root>/thread` through `monitorMattermostProvider`; a fake websocket only injected `posted` events into the monitor. The route/thread session key stayed stable while the stored thread `sessionId` rotated. Cold start included prior root/thread context, same-session server-only context stayed absent, and stored-thread-session reset included new server-only prior context:

target.title: feat(tui): inline image rendering via pi-tui Image component
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When tools generate images (charts, diagrams, AI art via `image_generate`), the TUI shows `[image/png 800kb]` text placeholders. Users can't see images without switching to another app.
- Why it matters: Breaks the flow during iterative visual work. The `image_generate` tool landed recently (`3a456678ee`, `21c2ba480a`) but there's no rendering surface for it in the TUI.
- What changed: TUI tool result boxes now render images inline on terminals that support Kitty or iTerm2 graphics protocols, using pi-tui's built-in `Image` component. All file I/O happens once in `setResult()` and is cached - `refresh()` does zero I/O.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Gateway, WebUI, verbose filter, image tools, parse.ts, media store. Only TUI rendering is touched. Non-image-capable terminals keep the existing text fallback with zero behavior change.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #23764, #36641, #36740 (prior attempts - 1700+ lines / 26 files, all closed)
- Depends on `3a456678ee` feat(image-generation): add image_generate tool
- Depends on `21c2ba480a` Image generation: native provider migration (#49551)

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

On terminals with Kitty or iTerm2 graphics support (Kitty, WezTerm, iTerm2): tool results containing `MEDIA:` image paths now render the image inline inside the tool result box. `MEDIA:` path text is stripped when the image renders visually.

On all other terminals (VS Code, Windows Terminal, Apple Terminal): no change. Existing `[image/png 800kb]` text placeholders are preserved.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No - reads local files that tools already wrote to disk. Validated with: absolute path check, `lstatSync` symlink rejection, image extension whitelist, 6MB size bound with TOCTOU guard, `path.normalize` before all checks.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11 / macOS / Linux
- Runtime/container: Node 22+
- Model/provider: Any provider with `image_generate` configured (Google, OpenAI, fal, xAI)
- Integration/channel (if any): TUI only
- Relevant config (redacted): `agents.defaults.imageGenerationModel` set (or auto-inferred since `0aff1c7630`)

### Steps

1. Open the TUI in a Kitty/WezTerm/iTerm2 terminal
2. Ask the agent to generate an image: "Generate an image of a sunset over mountains"
3. Wait for the `image_generate` tool to complete

### Expected

- Image renders inline inside the tool result box
- `MEDIA:` path text is not visible (replaced by the visual image)
- Expanding/collapsing the tool result attaches/detaches the image without delay

### Actual

- Before this PR: `[image/png]` text placeholder shown, no visual rendering

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

63 tests pass across 5 test files (24 inline-image security/capability tests + 14 tool-execution lifecycle tests + 25 existing TUI component tests). `pnpm check` passes all 15 linters.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Built worktree with `image_generate` on upstream/main, ran `pnpm check` (all pass), ran `vitest run src/tui/components/` (63/63 pass), verified `canRenderInlineImages()` detects WezTerm Kitty protocol support.
- Edge cases checked: symlink rejection, oversized files (>6MB), non-image extensions, null bytes in paths, relative paths, empty files, `..` traversal normalization, `setPartialResult` after `setResult` (stale cache clearing), double `setResult` (replacement).
- What you did **not** verify: Live end-to-end TUI rendering with actual image generation (waiting for stable main CI to do a full manual test).

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

No bot comments received yet (draft PR).

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert the single commit touching `src/tui/components/tool-execution.ts`. The `canRenderInlineImages()` gate means non-image terminals are never affected.
- Files/config to restore: `src/tui/components/tool-execution.ts` (restore to upstream version). Delete `src/tui/components/inline-image.ts` and test files.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Garbled escape sequences in tool output on terminals that falsely report Kitty/iTerm2 support. TUI freezing after tool result (would indicate sync I/O leaked into render path - but this is architecturally prevented by the setResult/refresh split).

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: pi-tui `getCapabilities()` falsely detects image support on a terminal that doesn't actually render Kitty/iTerm2 protocol, producing garbled escape sequences.
  - Mitigation: This is a pi-tui detection issue, not specific to this PR. The `Image` component already has a text fallback path. Any detection bug would affect all pi-tui image users, not just this feature.
- Risk: Large images (up to 6MB base64 = ~8MB string) cached per tool result. With many image-producing tool results visible, memory usage grows.
  - Mitigation: ChatLog prunes oldest components at 180 entries. Cached images are GC'd when their ToolExecutionComponent is removed. In practice, most sessions have fewer than 5 image-producing tool results visible at once.

target.title: fix(cron): preserve on-exit watchers across hot reload
target.body:
Closes #99709.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an on-exit cron watched command could be interrupted and re-executed when an unrelated `cron.*` config change triggered gateway hot reload.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron hot reload now stops cron scheduling without using the shutdown path that cancels watcher children. The rebuilt cron service reuses the existing watcher manager, including the production lazy cron state, refreshes its callbacks, and lets reconciliation cancel only removed or changed jobs.

## User Impact

Operators can edit cron configuration while a watched deploy, migration, or other long-running command is in flight without causing that command to run twice.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof: ran a synthetic on-exit job through the real lazy gateway cron state and real `createGatewayReloadHandlers().applyHotReload` path. The watched command was a real child process that appended to a temp marker file, slept, and exited; a duplicate arm would append a second marker. The proof pinned OpenClaw config/state to a temp directory.

```text
[reload] config hot reload applied (cron)
markerCountBeforeReload: 1
markerCountAfterRestartCronHotReload: 1
lazyExitWatchersExposed: true
watcherObjectReusedAcrossReload: true
activeBeforeReload: [same synthetic job id]
activeImmediatelyAfterReload: [same synthetic job id]
activeAfterCommandExit: []
finalJobEnabled: false
finalLastRunStatus: ok
finalLastRunAtMsType: number
RESULT: PASS - restartCron hot reload preserved the in-flight on-exit command, did not re-execute it, and the watcher completed the job once after exit.
```

target.title: fix(ui): chat workspace panel leaves an empty gap when collapsed
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the session workspace panel in the Control UI chat view wasted horizontal space on both sides of its toggle:

- **Collapsed**, it still reserved a 52px empty rail on the right edge — a permanent dead gap with two orphaned icons floating in it. The panel looked half-closed instead of closed.
- **Expanded**, it floated inside the content gutter with a rounded corner and a ~20px strip of dead background between the panel and the window edge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel now behaves like the docked terminal at the bottom of the shell:

- **Collapsed**: the workbench grid drops the rail column entirely (`minmax(0, 1fr)` single column) and the expand toggle floats over the chat's top-right corner as a small glass button, matching the existing circular nav-toggle pattern. The decorative file icon in the collapsed strip was removed along with its now-dead CSS.
- **Expanded**: the chat content area drops its right gutter and squares the card's right corners (guarded to viewports >1120px, where the rail actually renders), so the panel closes flush against the window edge.

The toggle keeps its accessible name (`Expand session workspace`) and `aria-expanded` state.

## User Impact

Closing the workspace panel gives the full width back to the chat; opening it docks the panel flush to the window edge like the terminal drawer. The expand control stays visible and clickable in the top-right corner, so the panel remains one click away.

## Evidence

**Before** — collapsed panel still reserves an empty rail (note the gap on the right edge):

![before: collapsed rail reserves an empty 52px column](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/workspace-rail-collapse/before-collapsed.png)

![after: collapsed rail takes no width, floating expand toggle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/workspace-rail-collapse/after-collapsed.png)

**After (expanded)** — the open panel docks flush to the window edge (no gutter, square corners), like the bottom terminal:

![after: expanded workspace rail docked flush to the window edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/workspace-rail-collapse/after-expanded.png)

target.title: feat(slack): add ignoreOtherMentions channel config
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In busy Slack rooms where `requireMention` is disabled, OpenClaw can respond to messages explicitly directed at another user or user group. This adds an opt-in per-channel filter for #89625 without changing default behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add `channels.slack.channels.<id>.ignoreOtherMentions`, matching the existing Discord configuration concept.
- Keep the decision in Slack's inbound owner, where native user and user-group mentions and the authenticated bot user ID are available.
- Treat Slack thread participation differently from Discord: participation is broad and does not count as an explicit bot mention for this filter.
- Preserve suppressed messages as pending channel history so later bot-directed turns retain useful context.
- Fail open when the bot user ID is unavailable rather than misclassifying a native mention.
- Keep TypeScript types, Zod schema, resolved channel config, generated metadata, config baselines, and Slack docs aligned.

## User Impact

The new option defaults to `false`. When enabled for a Slack channel or private channel, messages that mention another user or user group but not the bot are stored as pending context and are not handled. Bot-directed messages, ordinary unmentioned messages, DMs, and group DMs keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/slack/src/monitor/message-handler/prepare.test.ts` — 100 tests passed.
- Generated metadata and docs baseline checks passed.
- Fresh full-branch autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; best bounded fix, confidence 0.94.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwqracphtj8m49be5xmhpyxy` — broad changed gate passed in 10m16s: core/extension production and test types, lint, import cycles, state/storage guards, config guards, and changed-surface checks.
- Contributor live Slack proof: coworker-only mentions stopped triggering the bot inside a bot-participated thread; explicit bot mentions still triggered it.

Closes #89625.

target.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events
target.body:
### Summary

Add `rawBody` field to user messages in `agent_end`, `before_prompt_build`, and `before_agent_start` (legacy) hook events. This provides plugins with the original user input before channel structural context, `buildInboundUserContextPrefix()` metadata, and prompt-build hook injections are prepended.

### Motivation

Plugin hooks receive `event.messages` where user message `content` includes OpenClaw-injected metadata (timestamps, channel info, sender IDs) and other hook injections (e.g., memory context). Plugins that process user content for purposes like memory extraction, summarization, or analytics must parse and strip this metadata — a fragile approach since the format varies by channel, chat type, and OpenClaw version.

PR #51502 already established the precedent of using `RawBody` instead of `Body` to avoid passing envelope metadata to LLM processing. This PR extends that principle to plugin hook events.

### Changes

- Compute `rawBodyForHooks` from `CommandBody ?? RawBody ?? Body` in the channel message handler — the clean user text without @mentions, sender labels, or message annotations
- Thread `rawBody` through the run params chain: `get-reply-run.ts` → `runReplyAgent` → `runAgentTurnWithFallback` → `runEmbeddedPiAgent` → `runEmbeddedAttempt`
- Include `rawBody` in hook event objects for `before_prompt_build`, `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`
- Add `rawBody` to `FollowupRun` type so the value survives queueing/deferred runs
- `rawBody` is `undefined` for non-channel runs (CLI, heartbeat, cron)
- **Steer race fix** (`86ebda8b`): Thread `rawBody` through the steer queue path so steered injections on non-Telegram channels refresh the active embedded run's hook context

### Backward Compatibility

- Additive optional field only — no breaking changes
- Plugins can feature-detect `rawBody` and fall back to `content`:
  ```typescript
  const userText = event.rawBody ?? extractText(lastUser.content);
  ```
- Plugin SDK API baseline unchanged (no drift)

### Use Case

Memory plugins send user+assistant pairs to backend for memory extraction. Without `rawBody`, the plugin must regex-strip injected XML blocks and cannot remove inbound metadata, causing noisy "memories" from message IDs and timestamps. With `rawBody`, the plugin gets clean user input directly.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Plugin hook events (`before_prompt_build`, `agent_end`) now expose `event.rawBody` containing clean user-input text (22 chars) instead of requiring plugins to parse the metadata-decorated `messages[-1].content` (411 chars). Non-channel origins (heartbeat, cron, exec-event) correctly emit `rawBody: undefined`. Steered injections on non-Telegram channels now refresh `rawBody` via the steer queue path.

Real environment tested: Linux 6.17.0-1013-aws (arm64), Node v22.22.2, OpenClaw 2026.5.20, Bedrock `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (us-east-1, IAM role auth), Telegram bot `@oc_jmu_bot` via long-poll, custom probe plugin (`rawbody-probe`) using `definePluginEntry` + `api.on("before_prompt_build")` + `api.on("agent_end")`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Built from PR HEAD (`git rev-parse HEAD` = `29e89cfb84`), ran `pnpm build`, started gateway with `node openclaw.mjs gateway --allow-unconfigured --port 18799 --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`. Sent Telegram DM "hello rawbody test 004" to `@oc_jmu_bot`. Triggered heartbeat via `node openclaw.mjs system event --text "..." --mode now --url ws://127.0.0.1:18799 --token anonymous --json`. Ran unit tests: `pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts -t "rawBody hook gating" --reporter=verbose`.

Evidence after fix:
```
Case A — Channel happy path (Telegram DM):
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 4c1c5a9b-8e2c-405f-b6f3-d2246e4912cc
[rawbody-probe] trigger  = user
[rawbody-probe] rawBody  = "hello rawbody test 004"   (22 chars)
[rawbody-probe] lastUser = "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\n...
                            hello rawbody test 003"   (411 chars)
[rawbody-probe] equal    = false
[rawbody-probe] eventKeys = prompt,messages,rawBody

Case B — Heartbeat origin:
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 40d31407-6882-4f23-bdc7-85ba18fb5a41
[rawbody-probe] trigger  = heartbeat
[rawbody-probe] rawBody  = <undefined>
[rawbody-probe] lastUser = "[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]"
[rawbody-probe] eventKeys = messages,success,error,durationMs,rawBody,runId

Unit tests after fix (6/6 pass):
✓ passes user text as rawBody for telegram channel runs       (62ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for heartbeat runs               (2ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for cron-event runs              (1ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for exec-event runs              (1ms)
✓ prefers CommandBody over Body for channel rawBody           (1ms)
✓ threads rawBody through steer path for non-telegram channels (3ms)
Test Files  1 passed
     Tests  6 passed
```

Observed result after fix: `event.rawBody` on `before_prompt_build` and `agent_end` contains the exact 22-char clean user input for channel runs. Non-channel origins correctly emit `undefined`. The steer path unit test confirms `followupRun.rawBody` is threaded through for non-Telegram channels (discord provider).

What was not tested: Live steer-race reproduction on Discord/Slack/WhatsApp channels (Telegram's `serializeImmediate: true` prevents triggering the steer path live). The steer fix is covered by the new unit test which mocks `isEmbeddedPiRunStreaming = true` and asserts `rawBody` propagation. No multi-user concurrency test was performed.

target.title: feat(session): add chat-channel session switching with LRU history retention
target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: Chat channels did not support listing or switching between prior sessions under the same SessionKey, and follow-up fixes were needed to preserve switchable transcripts until LRU eviction and restore per-session usage/compaction snapshots correctly.
- Why it matters: Without in-chat session switching, users cannot navigate past conversations from Feishu/DingTalk/Telegram/Discord-style chat surfaces; incorrect transcript/archive or snapshot behavior would also make `/session back`, `/sessions`, and `/status`-adjacent state feel unreliable.
- What changed: Added `/sessions`, `/session <number>`, `/session <sessionId>`, and `/session back` for chat channels; introduced per-SessionKey LRU `sessionHistory`; preserved switchable transcripts until history eviction; restored token/context/compaction snapshots on switch; documented matching/order/retention behavior; cleaned up reset semantics so `session.historyLimit=0` truly disables switchable history.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): This PR does not change SessionKey routing, does not add cross-SessionKey switching, does not add named sessions/UI picker flows, and does not change channel plugin-specific transport behavior.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #9959
- Related #28168

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

List user-visible changes (including defaults/config).  
If none, write `None`.

- Added `/sessions` to list switchable sessions for the current chat SessionKey.
- Added `/session <number>`, `/session <sessionId>`, and `/session back` for in-chat session switching.
- Current session is included in `/sessions`, marked as `[current]`.
- `/sessions` now shows compact single-line preview rows with session ID prefix and truncated preview text.
- Session switching now restores stored token/context/compaction snapshots for the target session.
- `session.historyLimit` now consistently supports `0` as “disable switchable session history”.
- Transcripts for sessions still in history remain switchable; transcripts are archived when evicted from the LRU history queue.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux
- Runtime/container: local OpenClaw dev runtime / source tree
- Model/provider: N/A for core session-switch logic
- Integration/channel (if any): chat-channel command flow; manually validated in a real chat session
- Relevant config (redacted):
  - `session.historyLimit: 5` (default path)
  - `session.historyLimit: 0` (disable-history regression path)

### Steps

1. Start a chat conversation and create multiple sessions with `/new`.
2. Run `/sessions`, then switch via `/session <number>` or `/session back`.
3. Continue creating sessions until the history limit is exceeded.

### Expected

- `/sessions` lists current + recent switchable sessions in LRU order.
- Switching restores the target session’s stored metadata/snapshots.
- Sessions still present in history remain switchable.
- The oldest session is archived only after LRU eviction.
- With `session.historyLimit=0`, switchable history is disabled and the previous session is archived immediately on reset.

### Actual

- Behavior matches the expected results above in targeted tests and manual validation.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios:
  - `/sessions` output in chat
  - `/session back` restores the previous session
  - switching to a still-retained historical session restores expected context/state
  - LRU eviction archives only the oldest evicted session
  - daily reset path preserves switchable history
  - `session.historyLimit=0` disables switchable history and archives immediately on reset
- Edge cases checked:
  - history boundary behavior at the configured limit
  - selecting current session is a no-op
  - unique-prefix SessionId selection behavior
  - stale/daily-reset session rollover
- What you did **not** verify:
  - every individual chat provider/plugin surface
  - cross-SessionKey switching (out of scope)
  - any UI/card-based session picker (out of scope)

## Review Conversations

- [ ] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [ ] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps:

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly:
  - revert this PR, or set `session.historyLimit=0` to disable switchable session history
- Files/config to restore:
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`
  - `src/config/sessions/types.ts`
  - `src/config/types.base.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for:
  - `/sessions` shows stale/incorrect ordering
  - switched sessions lose expected token/context/compaction snapshot state
  - transcripts are archived too early while still present in history
  - `session.historyLimit=0` does not disable switchable history

## Risks and Mitigations

List only real risks for this PR. Add/remove entries as needed. If none, write `None`.

- Risk: LRU eviction/archive timing could regress and archive a session that should still remain switchable.
  - Mitigation: Added/updated targeted tests covering retained-history vs evicted-history behavior.

- Risk: Snapshot restore could leave token/context/compaction state inconsistent after switching.
  - Mitigation: Added lifecycle tests covering restore and missing-metadata fallback behavior.

- Risk: Docs could drift from implementation again as follow-up fixes land.
  - Mitigation: Updated `docs/design/chat-session-switch.md` to match the current implementation semantics in this PR.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted: Yes

I used an AI assistant for code review, doc cleanup, and targeted test updates. I manually reviewed the final diff, understood the changes, and verified the session-switch flows myself.

target.title: Fix nodejs installation logic on Debian-based systems
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where non-Arch Linux systems (such as Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, etc.) that happen to have a `pacman` executable present in their `PATH` were incorrectly routed into Arch-based installer branches.  
This caused the installer to attempt `pacman -Sy` operations on systems that do not use pacman as a package manager, breaking build-tool installation, Git installation, and the Node.js install path.

The root cause was that the Arch detection logic treated the presence of any `pacman` binary as proof of an Arch-based distribution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous logic relied on:

```
command -v pacman || is_arch_linux
```

Additionally, `is_arch_linux` itself included a fallback that returned success if `pacman` existed in `PATH`.  
This produced false positives whenever any package or program named `pacman` was installed on non-Arch systems.

To correct this:

1. **Removed the pacman fallback from `is_arch_linux()`**  
   The function now identifies Arch-based systems only via `/etc/os-release` or `/etc/arch-release`.

2. **Switched installer conditions from `||` to `&&`**  
   The installer now requires:
   - a system that is *actually* Arch-based  
   - and a real pacman package manager available  
   before using pacman installation paths.

This prevents unrelated binaries named `pacman` from triggering Arch-specific routes.

## User Impact

- Debian/Ubuntu/Mint users who have any program named `pacman` on their system (e.g., games or custom tools) will no longer be misdetected as Arch.
- Installer routes for build tools, Git, and Node.js now reliably use `apt`/NodeSource on Debian-based systems.
- Arch and Arch-like distributions continue to install packages via pacman normally.
- This change improves reliability and prevents package‑manager confusion in multi-distro setups and development environments.

## Evidence

(You will add your real logs + test outputs here as soon as you run the PR-proof steps.)

---

## Follow-up (optional)

Dear maintainers,  
If you agree, I can submit a separate PR to add distro‑specific helpers such as `is_debian_linux()` and `is_fedora_linux()` to reduce repeated `command -v apt-get` / `command -v dnf` checks and improve installer routing clarity across the codebase.

target.title: fix(security): use constant-time comparison for TLS fingerprint verification
target.body:
## Summary

TLS certificate fingerprint verification in `src/gateway/client.ts` uses `!==` (standard JavaScript string equality), which is vulnerable to **timing side-channel attacks** (CWE-208).

An attacker on the network path can measure response time differences to iteratively guess the correct fingerprint byte-by-byte, potentially bypassing TLS pinning for MITM attacks on gateway connections.

## Root cause

Two locations perform fingerprint comparison with `!==`:

| Location | Context |
|----------|---------|
| Line 205 | WebSocket `checkServerIdentity` callback |
| Line 681 | HTTP `validateTlsFingerprint` method |

## Fix

Replace both with `safeEqualSecret()` from `src/security/secret-equal.ts`, which uses `SHA-256` hashing + `crypto.timingSafeEqual` for constant-time comparison.

This is the **same function already used** for pairing token verification elsewhere in the codebase — just missed for TLS fingerprints.

```diff
- if (fingerprint !== expected) {
+ if (!safeEqualSecret(fingerprint, expected)) {
```

## Why safeEqualSecret and not raw timingSafeEqual

`timingSafeEqual` requires both buffers to have equal length, which would leak the length of the expected fingerprint. `safeEqualSecret` avoids this by hashing both values with SHA-256 first (producing fixed 32-byte digests), then comparing the digests in constant time.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — compiles cleanly
- [x] `pnpm check` — lint/format passes
- [x] Existing `safeEqualSecret` tests in `src/security/audit-extra.sync.test.ts` cover equal, unequal, different-length, and undefined inputs
- [x] No remaining `fingerprint !== expected` patterns in codebase

target.title: fix(infra): formatDuration rolls over near-boundary values to the nex…
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where session maintenance warning messages would display durations like "60 minutes" or "24 hours" instead of "1 hour" or "1 day". Values near a unit boundary (e.g. 59m30s, 23h59m30s) were formatted incorrectly because the raw millisecond value was compared against the unit threshold before rounding. ## Why This Change Was Made `formatDuration` in `session-maintenance-warning.ts` checked `ms >= threshold` with the raw float, then rounded. A value like 3,570,000 ms is below the 3,600,000 ms hour threshold, so it fell through to the minutes branch and printed "60 minutes" after rounding. Rounding first and then checking the threshold fixes the rollover. This matches the same pattern fix applied to `format-duration.ts` in #99978. ## User Impact Session maintenance warning messages now display correct human-readable durations. "older than 60 minutes" becomes "older than 1 hour", "older than 60 seconds" becomes "older than 1 minute", and so on. ## Evidence Terminal proof showing before/after behavior for all three rollover boundaries (59.5s, 59m30s, 23h59m30s): Three regression tests cover the rollover cases: - 59,500 ms → "1 minute" (was "60 seconds") - 3,570,000 ms → "1 hour" (was "60 minutes") - 86,370,000 ms → "1 day" (was "24 hours")

target.title: Fix nodejs installation logic on Debian-based systems
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where non-Arch Linux systems (such as Debian, Ubuntu, Mint, etc.) that happen to have a `pacman` executable present in their `PATH` were incorrectly routed into Arch-based installer branches.  
This caused the installer to attempt `pacman -Sy` operations on systems that do not use pacman as a package manager, breaking build-tool installation, Git installation, and the Node.js install path.

The root cause was that the Arch detection logic treated the presence of any `pacman` binary as proof of an Arch-based distribution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous logic relied on:

```
command -v pacman || is_arch_linux
```

Additionally, `is_arch_linux` itself included a fallback that returned success if `pacman` existed in `PATH`.  
This produced false positives whenever any package or program named `pacman` was installed on non-Arch systems.

To correct this:

1. **Removed the pacman fallback from `is_arch_linux()`**  
   The function now identifies Arch-based systems only via `/etc/os-release` or `/etc/arch-release`.

2. **Switched installer conditions from `||` to `&&`**  
   The installer now requires:
   - a system that is *actually* Arch-based  
   - and a real pacman package manager available  
   before using pacman installation paths.

This prevents unrelated binaries named `pacman` from triggering Arch-specific routes.

## User Impact

- Debian/Ubuntu/Mint users who have any program named `pacman` on their system (e.g., games or custom tools) will no longer be misdetected as Arch.
- Installer routes for build tools, Git, and Node.js now reliably use `apt`/NodeSource on Debian-based systems.
- Arch and Arch-like distributions continue to install packages via pacman normally.
- This change improves reliability and prevents package‑manager confusion in multi-distro setups and development environments.

## Evidence

(You will add your real logs + test outputs here as soon as you run the PR-proof steps.)

---

## Follow-up (optional)

Dear maintainers,  
If you agree, I can submit a separate PR to add distro‑specific helpers such as `is_debian_linux()` and `is_fedora_linux()` to reduce repeated `command -v apt-get` / `command -v dnf` checks and improve installer routing clarity across the codebase.

target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`
  - passed: `10 files / 170 tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`
  - passed: `0 warnings / 0 errors`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux using the actual `createHostWorkspaceWriteTool` implementation against a temporary workspace on the real filesystem.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a `node --import tsx` terminal smoke that created the host workspace write tool, wrote `first line`, reran the same write tool with `append: true` for `second line`, then read the resulting file.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the smoke:

  ```text
  workspace: $TMPDIR/openclaw-write-append-proof-.../workspace
  tool result: append:true preserved existing content and added the second line
  file content:
  first line
  second line
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The final file retained the original content and appended the new content in order; the append path did not truncate or replace the file.
- **What was not tested:** No live Gateway session was exercised; validation used the real tool implementation in an isolated local checkout plus targeted regression/type checks.

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.


### Current-head native app-server bridge proof (sanitized, 2026-07-03)

A current-head OpenClaw bridge proof was run with a disposable app-server home and a non-default entitlement fixture. This is intentionally classified as `PASS_CONTAMINATED_ONLY`; it validates the native app-server entitlement and OpenClaw bridge behavior, not clean-stage default-profile behavior. Production Gateway state and production config were not used.

```text
head: 78fb055d
live model/list target: gpt-5.6-sol
live supportedReasoningEfforts: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
thread/start: accepted, model=gpt-5.6-sol
turn/start: accepted
captured turn/start.effort: ultra
captured turn/start.collaborationMode.settings.reasoning_effort: ultra
cleanup: copied entitlement fixture absent after run
verdict: APP_SERVER_BRIDGE_ULTRA_OK
```

This directly exercises current-head OpenClaw source constructing a real native Codex app-server `turn/start` request after live discovery advertised Ultra.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets
target.body:
## Summary

ws 8.21.0 introduced `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` receiver limits (commit `[security] Limit retained message parts`) that can trigger `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and close connections with code 1008 under certain traffic patterns.

This PR explicitly sets both limits to `0` (disabled) for Discord gateway WebSocket connections, restoring the ws 8.20.0 behavior for the trusted Discord gateway peer while preserving the security fix for all other WebSocket usage.

## Changes

- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.ts`**: Base class `createWebSocket()` now passes `maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0` with a `ws.ClientOptions` cast (since `@types/ws` 8.18.1 does not yet expose these fields).
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.ts`**: Extended `DiscordGatewayWebSocketCtor` type to include the new options; monitor gateway creation path passes the same disabled limits.
- **`extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts`**: Added test verifying base class WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-plugin.test.ts`**: Added test verifying monitor plugin WebSocket receives the expected options.
- **`extensions/discord/src/monitor/provider.proxy.test.ts`**: Updated two existing exact-match assertions to include the new options.

## Why `0` instead of raising the limits

- ws 8.21.0 treats `0` as disabled (`receiver.js:61`, `receiver.js:98`: `if (this._maxBufferedChunks > 0 && ...)`), matching the pre-8.21.0 behavior exactly.
- Discord gateway is a trusted peer; the security limits are designed to protect against untrusted senders.
- Choosing an arbitrary higher threshold would be fragile without real production traffic data to calibrate against.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: ws 8.21.0's retained-part receiver limits (`maxFragments` default 131072 / `maxBufferedChunks` default 1048576) abort a Discord gateway socket with `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` / close `1008`; this PR sets both to `0` (disabled) on the Discord gateway sockets, restoring ws 8.20.0 behavior for that trusted peer.
- **Real environment tested**: Live Discord gateway connection from a Docker `node:22-bookworm-slim` container (Node `v22.22.3`) with the repo-pinned `ws@8.21.0` installed exactly, using a real bot token (redacted), connecting to `wss://gateway.discord.gg/?v=10&encoding=json`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: build a `node:22-bookworm-slim` image with `npm install ws@8.21.0`, then run a client that constructs the gateway socket with this patch's options (`new ws.WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 30000, maxBufferedChunks: 0, maxFragments: 0 })`), completes the HELLO/IDENTIFY/READY handshake against the real Discord gateway, sends heartbeats, holds a 60s stable window, then closes with code 1000.
- **Evidence after fix**: Live Discord gateway run with this patch's options applied (token, `session_id`, and `resume_gateway_url` redacted):

```
[env] node=v22.22.3 ws=8.21.0
[discord] connecting wss://gateway.discord.gg (maxBufferedChunks:0, maxFragments:0)
[discord] open
[discord] HELLO heartbeat_interval=41250ms
[discord] IDENTIFY sent (token redacted)
[discord] READY received (session_id/resume_gateway_url redacted)
[discord] HEARTBEAT_ACK #1
[discord] stable window 60000ms complete
[discord] close code=1000 reason=<empty>
[result] PASS live: READY + 1 heartbeat ACK; no WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS during stable window
```

Supplemental deterministic mechanism repro against a local ws 8.21.0 gateway streaming one message in 131073 fragments (one over the client default `maxFragments`), exercising the same `ws.WebSocket` receiver path:

```
# default ws.WebSocket (ws 8.21 defaults)
[before] open
[before] error code=WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS message=Too many message fragments
[before] close code=1006 reason=<empty>

# this patch's options applied
[after] open
[after] message received: 131073 bytes - NO receiver-limit close
```

- **Observed result after fix**: On the real Discord gateway, with the disabled limits applied, the connection reaches `READY`, exchanges heartbeats, and stays connected through the 60s window with no `WS_ERR_TOO_MANY_BUFFERED_PARTS` and no `1008` close; the only close is the intentional client-initiated `1000`. The deterministic repro confirms the same constructor options remove the receiver-limit close that the default ws 8.21 client hits.
- **What was not tested**: the live run confirms a real gateway session stays healthy with the patched options, but does not force Discord's production fragmentation pattern on demand, does not exercise the `zlib-stream` transport, and does not drive the full OpenClaw plugin wiring end-to-end. The deterministic repro proves the ws 8.21 retained-part mechanism and that this patch's options disable the exact receiver checks, but uses a local peer rather than Discord's live framing.

## Tests

- `gateway.test.ts`: 25 passed
- `gateway-plugin.test.ts`: 17 passed  
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: 21 passed
- TypeScript check (tsgo): clean

Fixes #88330

target.title: Prevent repeated byte-triggered compactions
target.body:
## Summary

- prevent repeated byte-triggered preflight compactions for the same active transcript when a previous byte-triggered compaction did not materially reduce the transcript below the configured threshold
- record byte-triggered compaction retry state on `SessionEntry` so retries require the same threshold, the same active session file, and material new growth
- preserve token-triggered preflight compaction behavior, including token compaction taking precedence when the byte retry is suppressed

## What Problem This Solves

When `agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes` is configured, a byte-triggered preflight compaction can legitimately leave the active successor transcript above the threshold (for example when transcript rotation preserves branch/state history). Without retry hysteresis, the next turn can immediately trigger another byte-based preflight compaction, producing a repeated compaction loop.

This patch records the post-compaction active transcript size/file/threshold for byte-triggered compactions and suppresses another byte-triggered retry for that same active transcript until it grows materially. A retry is allowed when the active file changes, the threshold changes, or the transcript grows by at least `max(1 MiB, 10%)` from the previously recorded byte size.

Token-triggered compaction remains unchanged.

## Related

Adjacent to #88188 because both involve `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` behavior, but this PR handles the opposite failure mode: byte-triggered preflight compaction firing repeatedly after a prior byte-triggered compaction leaves the active transcript above threshold.

## Real setup tested

Staged runtime validation in a clean upstream checkout on the current branch. The proof harness used a temporary session store/transcript file, called the real `runPreflightCompactionIfNeeded` runtime path, and replaced only the compaction executor with a recording stub so the trigger/skip decision still came from the production preflight guard. No production runtime or private deployment state was used for PR validation.

## Exact steps or command run after this patch

From the repository checkout:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.ts \
  src/config/sessions/types.ts \
  src/plugins/session-entry-slot-keys.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts

git diff --check

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts -- --run

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs \
  -p tsconfig.core.json \
  --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-byteguard.tsbuildinfo
```

## Evidence

- `agent-runner-memory.test.ts`: 53 tests passed
- `session-updates.test.ts` + `session-updates.lifecycle.test.ts`: 5 tests passed
- `tsgo` core project check passed
- formatting check passed
- diff whitespace check passed

New coverage includes:

- first byte-threshold crossing still triggers preflight compaction
- same active transcript + same threshold + no material growth suppresses repeated byte-triggered compaction
- changed active session file does not suppress retry
- changed threshold does not suppress retry
- material transcript growth allows retry
- token-triggered compaction still runs when byte retry is suppressed
- rotated successor file and byte size are recorded after byte-triggered compaction
- byte-triggered metadata is persisted through `incrementCompactionCount`
- ordinary token compactions do not write byte-triggered retry metadata

## Observed result after fix

The repeated byte-trigger retry condition is blocked for the same active transcript until there is material new growth, while token-triggered compaction and legitimate byte retries remain available.

Additional staged runtime proof from `tmp/pr-95885-proof/run-preflight-compaction-proof.ts` on head `bba688c7bc9de4aa9d511591a4b1a77b7ddacb34`:

```json
{"step":"byte-trigger first preflight","compactCallsBefore":0,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"transcript_bytes","currentTokenCount":124,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"byte-trigger same transcript retry","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":1,"compactedThisStep":false,"sessionId":"byte-session","compactionCount":1,"transcriptBytesCompactionBytes":487,"transcriptBytesCompactionThreshold":128}
{"step":"token-trigger still compacts","compactCallsBefore":1,"compactCallsAfter":2,"compactedThisStep":true,"trigger":"tokens","currentTokenCount":902,"sessionId":"token-session","compactionCount":1}
{"proof":"summary","totalCompactCalls":2,"triggers":["transcript_bytes","tokens"]}
```

This covers the runtime behavior ClawSweeper requested: the first byte-threshold crossing still compacts, the same active transcript/threshold retry is suppressed when there is no material growth, and token-triggered compaction still runs.


## What was not tested

- No production runtime or private deployment state was used.
- This PR does not change successor transcript pruning semantics; it only prevents immediate retry loops when a byte-triggered compaction does not materially shrink the active transcript.
- End-to-end UI notification behavior is not changed or tested here.

target.body:
Closes #99069

## Maintainer Note

TokenPlan support is intentionally included in this PR. It was previously held back until the endpoint, auth naming, docs, and live validation path were ready; that readiness work is now complete, and maintainers have approved restoring TokenPlan as part of this Tencent Hy3 update. ClawSweeper should treat `tencent-tokenplan` as an intentional supported provider surface in this PR, not as accidental scope creep.

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach current Tencent Hunyuan `hy3` through the supported OpenClaw provider/setup surfaces. The old plugin only exposed TokenHub `hy3-preview`, so onboarding, auth env detection, provider catalog discovery, docs, and config validation did not provide a complete path for `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit Tencent Hy3 support for both official endpoint families:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview`, `hy3`
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding choices: `tokenhub-api-key`, `tokenplan-api-key`
- Direct onboarding flags: `--tokenhub-api-key`, `--tokenplan-api-key`

TokenPlan intentionally uses the same short env-var naming convention as TokenHub: `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`, not `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

- Users can select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan through normal model refs and onboarding.
- TokenPlan works through `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` without manual provider config.
- Overlay-only provider config such as `models.providers.tencent-tokenplan.timeoutSeconds` validates like other built-in provider overlays.
- `hy3-preview` remains available on TokenHub.

## Evidence

Current PR head: `5b757c92b3ac2fa3433e76bf49b04a2c82fd6f6e`.

- `rg -n "TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY" .` — no matches; TokenPlan uses `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` only.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/config-misc.test.ts extensions/tencent/index.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts src/infra/dotenv.test.ts` — passed 4 Vitest shards, 186 tests.
- `pnpm check:docs` — passed: docs formatting, markdownlint, MDX, i18n glossary, link audit, and docs map check. Rerun after glossary cleanup at `bb3d31c`.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` — first run found missing TokenPlan built-in overlay validation; fixed in `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts` with coverage in `src/config/config-misc.test.ts`; rerun clean with no accepted/actionable findings.
- `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 OPENCLAW_ENABLE_PRIVATE_QA_CLI=1 OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=0 OPENCLAW_QA_REDACT_PUBLIC_METADATA=1 OPENCLAW_QA_TRANSPORT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=180000 node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-reply --channel-driver crabline --channel telegram --concurrency 1 --output-dir .artifacts/qa-e2e/pr-99076-message-tool-stranded-after-main-merge` — passed 1/1; verifies the previously failing QA Smoke scenario after merging latest `origin/main`.
- GitHub CI on current PR head `6984465cc52735c251996bf10695ddff9321eca4`: run `28699904711` completed successfully, including `QA Smoke CI`, `check-docs`, compact Node shards, lint, guards, test types, and build artifacts.

Supplementary verification / Docker Crabbox — Tencent TokenHub doctor/config repair and model-selection consistency (additional verification targeting old-config upgrade and model selection consistency):

- Focused tests (worktree `.worktrees/pr-99076` on head `706ac8245be`):
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tencent/config-compat.test.ts src/plugins/setup-registry.tencent.test.ts extensions/tencent/index.test.ts` — passed 2 Vitest shards, 14 tests (4 config-compat + 1 setup-registry + 9 index). Covers all four repair scenarios plus setup-registry dispatch.
- Docker Crabbox verification command (Docker backend only):
  `bash scripts/e2e/tencent-tokenhub-doctor-repair-docker.sh` — builds the `bare` OpenClaw Docker E2E image (`openclaw-tencent-tokenhub-doctor-e2e:latest`, image id `a374531c7bd5`) from `scripts/e2e/Dockerfile` target `bare`, bind-mounts the repo at `/repo` (read-only), sets `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR=/repo/extensions`, and runs `node scripts/e2e/tencent-tokenhub-doctor-repair-probe.mjs` inside the container against the prebuilt `dist/` bundles. Exit code `0`; final output `Tencent TokenHub doctor/config repair Docker E2E passed.`
- Doctor/config repair three scenarios (probe exercises the same migration path as `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-core-migrate.ts:87` calling `runPluginSetupConfigMigrations`, which dispatches to the Tencent plugin's `normalizeCompatibilityConfig` via the setup registry):
  1. Old preview-only config (`agents.defaults.model.primary = "tencent-tokenhub/hy3-preview"`, `models["tencent-tokenhub/hy3-preview"] = {}`) → after repair `primary = "tencent-tokenhub/hy3"`, `models` contains both `tencent-tokenhub/hy3` and `tencent-tokenhub/hy3-preview`; `hy3-preview` retained as optional. PASS.
  2. Intermediate hy3-only config (`primary = "tencent-tokenhub/hy3"`, `models["tencent-tokenhub/hy3"] = {}`) → after repair `models` adds `tencent-tokenhub/hy3-preview`; `primary` unchanged. PASS.
  3. No allowlist config (`models.providers.tencent-tokenhub` only, no `agents.defaults.models`) → after repair no `agents.defaults.models` is fabricated; `changes` empty. PASS.
- Idempotency: re-running repair on the scenario-1 and scenario-2 repaired configs reports zero `changes`; already-repaired config (scenario 4) also reports zero `changes`. PASS.
- Model selection data source: `buildModelsProviderData(repairedConfig, undefined, { view: "all" })` (the `/models` browse data builder, no picker bypass or allowlist bypass) → `byProvider.get("tencent-tokenhub")` contains `hy3` and `hy3-preview` (`models=[hy3,hy3-preview]`). PASS.
- Probe source: `scripts/e2e/tencent-tokenhub-doctor-repair-probe.mjs`; runner: `scripts/e2e/tencent-tokenhub-doctor-repair-docker.sh`. No secrets printed. Non-fatal `[plugins] ... failed to load` lines during `buildModelsProviderData` plugin discovery are read-only mount `EACCES` warnings for unrelated plugins (deepinfra, github-copilot, ollama, openai, xiaomi); the Tencent plugin loads and all five scenarios pass.

openclaw2 validation/deploy evidence:

- Core exact-ref deploy completed for `80b40a8535907e966ed0c5456958b3cb927e864e`: `OpenClaw 2026.7.4 (80b40a8)`, gateway healthy. Later commits are docs metadata plus config overlay validation; the Tencent plugin runtime package was separately built from current head.
- `OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_PACK_OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-pr-99076-pack bash scripts/plugin-clawhub-publish.sh --pack extensions/tencent` — packed `openclaw-tencent-provider-2026.6.11.tgz`, sha256 `267b1aa16013f2a2a65bae52708a56b92f1168724392f153aca35e43bf6914c5`.
- Installed that package on openclaw2 with `openclaw plugins install --force /tmp/openclaw-tencent-provider-pr-99076.tgz`; gateway restarted healthy; plugin `tencent` loaded from `~/.openclaw/extensions/tencent/dist/index.js` with providers `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`.
- Current openclaw2 live TokenPlan proof with the final auth name: `openclaw agent --agent main --model tencent-tokenplan/hy3 --message "Reply exactly: OK-TENCENT-TOKENPLAN-HY3" --timeout 180 --json` returned `OK-TENCENT-TOKENPLAN-HY3`; run id `3c5b772e-f2f3-45ad-b22c-41bed5289a72`, `provider=tencent-tokenplan`, `model=hy3`, `agentHarnessId=openclaw`, usage recorded. The key source was `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`; `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` is not used.
- Current openclaw2 live TokenHub proof: `openclaw agent --agent main --model tencent-tokenhub/hy3 --message "Reply exactly: OK-TENCENT-TOKENHUB-HY3" --timeout 180 --json` returned `OK-TENCENT-TOKENHUB-HY3`; run id `0c6427b3-ccd1-4b91-9b35-f34cb9ae761e`, `provider=tencent-tokenhub`, `model=hy3`, `agentHarnessId=openclaw`, usage recorded. The key source was `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`.

Supplementary Tencent TokenHub `reasoning_effort` live API probe (Docker, secret-safe, 2026-07-04):

- Key source: `openclaw2` `~/.openclaw/gateway.systemd.env` `TOKENHUB_API_KEY` (length 51), fetched via SSH command substitution into a one-shot env var. Never printed, written to a file, or persisted. Docker runtime: `node:24-bookworm-slim` image `sha256:242549cd46785b480c832479a730f4f2a20865d61ea2e404fdb2a5c3d3b73ecf` (same base as `scripts/e2e/Dockerfile` `bare`). Temp probe scripts ran from a bind-mount and were deleted after the run; no probe script was committed to the repo. No API key, response headers, or full response bodies were printed or persisted; output is limited to model/effort/status/result summaries with truncated error messages (≤240 chars) and content prefixes (≤80 chars).
- Endpoint: `https://tokenhub.tencentmaas.com/v1/chat/completions`; prompt: short user message; `max_tokens: 8` (acceptance probe) or `64` (reasoning-content probe); `stream: false`.

hy3 live reasoning_effort acceptance (model=`hy3`):

| model | reasoning_effort | HTTP status | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3 | high | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 |
| hy3 | none | 200 | ok; no reasoning_content; reasoning_tokens=0 (reasoning disabled) |
| hy3 | low | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats low as high) |
| hy3 | medium | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats medium as high) |
| hy3 | minimal | 200 | ok; reasoning_content present; reasoning_tokens=64 (server treats minimal as high) |

- Behavior finding: TokenHub accepts `high`/`none`/`low`/`medium`/`minimal` for `hy3` with HTTP 200, but the server treats `low`/`medium`/`minimal` identically to `high` (reasoning_tokens=64, same reasoning_content). Only `none` disables reasoning (reasoning_tokens=0). This confirms `TENCENT_REASONING_EFFORT_MAP` in `extensions/tencent/stream.ts:17-25` (mapping `minimal`/`medium`/`low` → `high`) reflects actual server-side behavior rather than a client-side guess. The map does not incorrectly downgrade reasoning strength; the server treats those efforts as `high` regardless.

hy3-preview live verification — blocked by gateway permission:

| model | reasoning_effort | HTTP status | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hy3-preview | (bare, no effort field) | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | high | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | low | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | none | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | minimal | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | medium | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |
| hy3-preview | no_think | 400 | err_code=401006 err_type=gateway_error "model hy3-preview not in allowed list" |

- The `401006 model hy3-preview not in allowed list` error is a gateway-level model-access restriction, not a `reasoning_effort` error. `/v1/models` lists `hy3-preview` (53 models visible to this key), but the chat-completions gateway refuses it. Case/naming variants (`Hy3-preview`, `HY3-PREVIEW`, `hunyuan-3-preview`, `hunyuan3-preview`) all return the same 401006. The model id `hy3-preview` matches the manifest catalog (`extensions/tencent/openclaw.plugin.json`) and the openclaw2 OpenClaw CLI, which also rejects `tencent-tokenhub/hy3-preview` with "Model override ... is not allowed for agent main". This is a TokenHub account permission restriction on the `openclaw2` key, not an OpenClaw code issue. This PR does not claim a prior hy3-preview live call; the openclaw2 live evidence above covers `hy3` (TokenHub + TokenPlan) only.
- Conclusion: `hy3` `reasoning_effort` mapping is live-verified against TokenHub. `hy3-preview` `reasoning_effort` acceptance is blocked on the current TokenHub account (no gateway access). Fully verifying the preview catalog's `["none","low","high"]` efforts requires a TokenHub key with `hy3-preview` completions access. The `stream.ts` code path that defers `minimal`/`medium` to the shared model fallback (resolving to `low` via `src/agents/openai-reasoning-effort.ts:152,164`) is internally consistent with the `reasoning_effort` spec, but cannot be live-confirmed under the current credentials.

CI failure note:

- The earlier `QA Smoke CI` failure was in `message-tool-stranded-final-reply` under Crabline Telegram local-provider proof, not Tencent provider code. This branch does not carry QA harness or Telegram changes.
- The branch was updated to latest `origin/main`, which already contains the QA/Crabline fix; the focused scenario passes locally, and current-head GitHub `QA Smoke CI` passed in run `28699904711`.
- The later `check-docs` failure was related to this PR's docs changes: `docs/docs_map.md` was stale and the zh-CN glossary lacked the new Tencent labels. Both are fixed and `pnpm check:docs` passes locally.

Docs updated in the same PR:

- `docs/providers/tencent.md` — provider table, auth env vars, onboarding flags, model matrix
- `docs/plugins/reference/tencent.md` — models / auth reference
- `docs/providers/index.md`, `docs/plugins/plugin-inventory.md` — index entries; Tencent provider label now uses the same `Tencent Cloud (TokenHub / TokenPlan)` wording as the page title
- `docs/docs_map.md`, `docs/.i18n/glossary.zh-CN.json` — generated docs map and glossary metadata required by `check-docs`; duplicate Tencent Cloud TokenHub/TokenPlan glossary variants were removed
